output:
La Chaux-de-Fonds, 1er janvier 1900

Monsieur l'Inspecteur,

You will come back this morning and I shall be here. I write first so that what I did is set down in my own words, before the town sets it down in its own.

On the night of the 31st I struck Aurèle Monnier from behind with the brass mallet from his bench. I did it at 22:38, in the atelier, while Odile was playing in the salon for me.

The reason is Jules Monnier. In 1889 I attended him in his last illness. I gave him laudanum for a bad night and went on giving it after I should have stopped. He died of it. I signed the certificate as heart failure, and no one ever asked me to account for it, so no one did.

In December Aurèle found Jules's last letter among his brother's papers. It described the doses. He read there what I had done. Before dinner, in the hall, he told me that he would tell Félix at midnight and the authorities after. He said that at the turn of the century he settled his accounts. He was a man who did what he said he would do, and I had known him for thirty years.

I went up the two flights while the piano covered my steps. He was at his bench with the repeater in his hand. I struck him once. He fell and pressed the slide, and I heard it and counted it, as anyone in this town would. Ten low notes, two doubled, eight high: 10:38.

I then stopped the regulator and set its hands back to five minutes past ten, an hour I had spent at cards in Odile's sight. I went down, took my cigar case from my coat in the hall, and was back in the salon at 22:46. Odile stopped playing when I came in. She knew nothing of the rest, and I ask you to say so plainly to anyone who suggests otherwise.

I told you I left the salon at a quarter to eleven by my watch. I said that because I wished you to believe the repeater had already sounded before I went up. My watch ran two minutes fast all evening. I should have told you so, and I did not.

I have told you everything else as it was. I have not been a careful liar. I have been a careful physician, which is a different thing and a worse one to be found out as.

Félix, I am sorry. You must be told this from me and not from a newspaper. Your father's death was my doing, and your uncle meant to give you the truth at midnight. It was I who prevented him. The letter that explains your father's last months is among Aurèle's papers. Read it before you judge anyone else's motives, including mine.

Girard was in the street that night, and so, I think, was Félix's brandy in the library; I did not think of either when I went up the stairs. Lina Ruedi was sent down before any of this began, and she is the best hand in that atelier. Rosa has never in her life been late for anything, and I did not consider that she might hear a piano and know its hour.

Tempora mutantur. I have been slow to notice it, and quicker than I should have been to act as though the old rules still applied to me.

I shall not ask for anything. I have no claim left to make.

Casimir Vauthier
docteur en médecine
